geo_text: Pinnacle Glaivier is the stance-switching identity. The class alternates between Flurry stance (wide AoE glaive sweeps) and Focus stance (narrow spear thrusts). Switching stances at full Identity Gauge provides: Focus switch → +20% damage +50% crit damage +15% move speed; Flurry switch → +15% damage +25% crit chance +15% attack speed. The identity is built around maximizing stance switches and using each stance's skills before switching back.

economy.plain_text: DUAL STANCE GAUGE: Each stance has its own gauge (Focus Gauge, Flurry Gauge). Using skills in each stance fills that stance's gauge. When a gauge is FULL and you switch stances, you receive a stance-switch buff: Focus (full) → switch to Flurry → Flurry buff applies (+15% dmg, +25% crit, +15% atk speed). Flurry (full) → switch to Focus → Focus buff applies (+20% dmg, +50% crit dmg, +15% mv speed). PINNACLE IDENTITY: these buffs are substantially enhanced vs no-engraving. The goal is maintaining both buffs simultaneously by switching as soon as each gauge fills.

mechanics_notes: 1) Pinnacle is LA's clearest example of 'stance-switching as primary identity mechanic.' The design philosophy: you play BOTH halves of the class simultaneously, each half charging the other's buff. This is a 'meta-skill' identity where the skill expression is WHEN to switch rather than WHICH skill to use. 2) Dual-footprint across stance is unique: the class literally changes its hit geometry by switching stance. Wide AoE glaive → narrow spear thrust is a geometry mode-switch on demand. 3) CORPUS NOTE: Glaivier's dual-stance system is a potential mechanic reference for any engine design involving stance/form switches with distinct hit geometries. No other corpus class has this exact geometry-mode-switch mechanic. 4) Pinnacle vs Control: Pinnacle embraces dual-stance complexity; Control locks to Focus stance only for simpler but powerful single-stance output. Same base class, dramatically different complexity profile.
